name: Garden multifamily
summary: 2-4 story Type V wood-frame walk-ups on surface parking - the lowest-cost multifamily product; cost is driven by framing, MEP, finishes and a meaningful (~12-14%) on-site development share. Good data: an elemental breakdown from RAND (Trammell Crow Residential garden projects), RLB city ranges, RSMeans, a Florida HFA hard-cost factor and several developer/contractor ranges; per-unit market-rate data are thinner than per-SF data.

typicalSize.method: Typical suburban garden community of 8-15 three-story buildings; Apers' worked example uses 200 units and RAND's weighted basic project is 185 units (garden-dominated). Range reflects common lender/institutional deal sizes.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross building SF per unit incl. breezeways and clubhouse share. Census median new rental unit = 1,000 net SF (e14, all types); garden units run at or above the median and open breezeways keep gross/net near 1.05-1.10.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Apers and LandSouth both cite 15-30 units/acre for garden; mid = midpoint rounded.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Apers: '1.5–2.0 spaces per unit, surface, uncovered'; mid set slightly below midpoint reflecting typical 1.6-1.75 suburban zoning minimums.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Per-unit = perSF x sfPerPrimaryUnit: mid $185/SF x 1,050 SF = ~$195k; low $145-155 x 900 = ~$140k; high $240-250 x 1,200 = ~$290k. Cross-checks (2026 $): Terrapin garden walk-up $195-265k (e7, contractor, higher-cost markets); Florida LIHTC hard-cost factor $256k (e12, a cap); Apers' worked example ~$184k/unit hard. RAND 2019 Texas garden (e8) is a low-cost anchor used only as a ratio check (older dollars, not escalated by hand).

perSF.method: 2026-dollar evidence for vertical hard cost: LandSouth $130-190 (e5), Apers $150-210 (e6), Terrapin $185-285 residential SF (e7); RLB's all-multifamily range in low-cost metros starts at $195-205 (e2, e3) and RLB/RSMeans ranges (e1, e4) span all multifamily product so mark the upper bound. Vertical midpoint ~$165-170/SF; add ~11-13% for on-site work (sitework + onsite land development + landscaping + amenities = 13.7% of hard cost in RAND garden table, e8) => mid ~$185/GSF incl. sitework. Low/high = low-cost Sun Belt suburban vs. higher-cost metro garden product. Older evidence (e13, 2018 Denver) used only as a spread check.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P, on-site work (grading, paving/surface parking, on-site utilities, landscaping, pool/amenity hardscape) and clubhouse shell/finish; excludes land, soft costs, FF&E, off-sites, impact/tap fees and financing.

qualityTiers.method: Spread from finish-level evidence: Terrapin 3-story market-rate vs affordable ($290-425k vs $230-340k, ~+25%, e7); EVstudio amenities +$10/SF (~+7%, e13); LA premium finish $350+ vs basic $250-280 (+25-40%, e18). Economy = no-amenity, value-engineered walk-up (~-15%).

systemSplit.method: Mapped from RAND Table 3.4 Texas garden-project spending per NRSF (e8; 21 categories = ~95% of hard cost): GC general conditions + GC fee -> 01; foundations -> 03; masonry & cladding split 50/50 -> 04/07; misc steel -> 05; framing -> 06; roofing -> 07; windows -> 08; drywall + painting + flooring -> 09; appliances -> 11; cabinets -> 12; plumbing -> 22; HVAC -> 23; electrical -> 26; sitework + 30% of onsite land development -> 31; 40% of onsite land development + landscaping + site amenity package -> 32; 30% of onsite land development -> 33. The listed categories were scaled to 95% and the unlisted ~5% (doors/hardware, insulation, sprinklers, specialties, low-voltage, fire alarm, trim) allocated by judgment: 08 +1.0%, 07 +1.0%, 21 +1.2%, 10 +0.5%, 27 +0.4%, 28 +0.4%, 06 +0.5%.

lineItems.name: On-site land development (grading, paving, on-site utilities)

cost.method: RAND Table 3.4 onsite land development per NRSF: Texas $8.84 (mid), California $9.83 (high); low is judgment for flat, simple sites. 2019 Texas dollars; build script escalates/regionalizes.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline; priced per net rentable SF, qty assumes NRSF ~= 0.9 x gross SF.

lineItems.name: Site amenity package (pool, dog park, grills, playground)

cost.method: RAND Table 3.4 site amenity package per NRSF: Texas $1.98 (mid), California $4.09 (high, CA dollars). 2019 Texas dollars.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline; priced per NRSF, qty assumes NRSF ~= 0.9 x gross SF.

lineItems.name: Clubhouse / leasing center with fitness (3,000-6,000 SF)

cost.method: Derived: 3,000-6,000 SF at roughly 1.2-1.5x the residential $/SF (commercial kitchen-lite, fitness, higher finish) ~= $250-370/SF in 2026 dollars.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; already inside the per-unit baseline for a ~250-unit community.

lineItems.name: Surface parking (asphalt, striping, lighting, drainage share)

cost.method: Derived: ~330-400 SF of paving per space incl. drive aisle x ~$11-18/SF for subgrade, base, asphalt, curb, striping and lighting (2026). Verify against _blocks/parking.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; garden baseline assumes surface parking.

cost.method: Derived: pre-engineered steel carport canopies ~ $3-6.5k per stall incl. footings and lighting (2026); common in Sun Belt garden product.
Derived: ~250-280 SF wood-frame garage stall on slab at ~$60-110/SF incl. door and electrical (2026).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: clubhouse, fitness, leasing and pool furniture/equipment for a ~250-unit community of ~$250-600k total = ~$1,000-2,500 per unit (2026). In-unit appliances are in hard cost (RAND e8 lists appliances inside hard cost).

pctOfHard.method: RAND market-rate soft/hard ratios: TX 0.19, CO 0.19 (efficient institutional developer, includes financing), CA 0.33 (e15). Brookings: soft 20-30% of total cost incl. financing (e16) => ~0.30-0.45 of hard. Because the engine treats construction interest separately, mid set at 0.22 (A&E, permits/fees, legal, insurance, taxes, marketing/lease-up, developer overhead) with the range bracketing RAND's state ratios. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 5 points: the RAND ratios it rests on include developer costs (~3 pts) and permits/fees (~2 pts). The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Garden A&E is lower than mid/high-rise (repetitive buildings). Impact fees vary widely: RAND reports averages of <$1,000/unit (TX), ~$12,000 (CO), ~$29,000 (CA) - model them separately.

design.method: Derived industry norm: 5% at schematic, falling to ~3% at CDs for repetitive garden product.

hard.method: Derived industry norm for wood-frame residential under GMP: 3-7% owner hard-cost contingency.

soft.method: Derived industry norm: 5% of soft costs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $140k x 1.10 (lean soft) ~= $155k; hard high $290k x 1.40 (high soft + contingency) ~= $405k; rounded. RAND 2019 TDC/unit incl. land for market-rate TX $122k / CO $193k (2019 $) sits below/inside this once escalated.
